title: What Does One More AI Agent Contribute? A Microeconomic Review of Delegation, Search, and Verification
abstract: What does a project gain when one more person sends an AI agent to work on it? We review the microeconomics of delegation, innovation contests, public goods, information, and market design through recent cases in mathematics, physics, biomedical research, software, and exchange. An extra attempt at an open problem can expand the set of solutions, improve an input that others use, or supply a second opinion. Each activity has a different return to entry. The contest literature emphasizes the diversity of attempts, the economics of cumulative innovation emphasizes downstream reuse, and information economics asks what a second report reveals conditional on the first. Which return a project can capture also depends on who supplies review and what the acceptance rule measures. Comparing a public proof desk with evidence extraction for rare diseases illustrates why duplicate work can waste resources in one assignment and be the purpose of another. We propose ways to distinguish these mechanisms using assignment, audit, and reuse records.
